notes: COPE (cope.es) DONE: 8100 unique URLs, 31/31 days in 2026-09-25..2026-10-25 (09-30=375, 10-10=125, 10-20=314, min 96 on 10-12), 3 HTTP requests, ~2 s runtime. Route: robots.txt (200, permissive -- only /search/ and /wp-admin/ disallowed, no Sitemap: line) -> /sitemap-index.xml (200, 345-entry sitemapindex) -> the two per-month news files it names, /sitemap-noticias-202609.xml.gz (200, 8153 entries, 1677 in window) and /sitemap-noticias-202610.xml.gz (200, 6788 entries, 6423 in window), both flat <urlset> with <lastmod>. The script derives the month files from the window and probes them directly too, so it survives the index changing. KEY: on cope.es <lastmod> IS the publication stamp, not an edit time -- it equalled the page JSON-LD "datePublished" to the second on 14/14 re-fetched articles spread over 09-29..10-22, so the lastmod date-part is the listed date. All 8100 URLs are .html articles (no video/podcast/image paths in the window), so no filtering was needed. Avoid: /sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml are 404, /news-sitemap.xml 404, and /wp-json/wp/v2/posts is 404 despite the WordPress-looking robots.txt (the CMS is not WP-REST). /sitemap-google-news.xml exists but only holds the last ~2 days, useless for a 31-day window. Verification: 4 samples re-fetched (one per target day) returned 200 with 6191-7025 chars of text and page dates exactly equal to the listed dates; 10 further random samples 200, 6212-9222 chars, dates within 1 day. No Wayback/GDELT fallback needed.
